findings.title: Metrics poll never populates MetricsStore; no component owns the per-tick push + sampled-rule evaluation loop
findings.location: PM2 integration layer (periodic poll), Metrics store, Alert engine (Sampled rules)
findings.problem: The poll 'feeds the MetricsStore' and sampled rules are 'checked on each poll tick', but no module owns the loop that runs every METRICS_SAMPLE_SEC, maps each ProcessSnapshot to a MetricSample, calls MetricsStore.push, and triggers AlertEngine sampled-rule evaluation. push takes a single sample while list yields an array; who maps and supplies ts is unspecified. Without this, cpu/mem threshold rules (AC12) cannot fire.
findings.fix: Have Pm2Client emit a metrics:tick event with the fresh ProcessSnapshot[] after each successful list(); MonitorState subscribes to push samples (ts=lastUpdated, cpu, mem=memory); AlertEngine subscribes to run sampled-rule evaluation. Specify behavior for non-online/deleted processes (skip push or push zeros; drop samples for deleted names).

findings.title: Per-rule error-spike/restart-threshold window length vs the tracker's single fixed sliding window is unmapped
findings.location: Error tracker (sliding-window counters, restart-window counter), alert-rule schema (error-spike withinSec, restart-threshold withinMin)
findings.problem: Each rule specifies its own window (withinSec / withinMin) and multiple rules with different windows can coexist, but the tracker keeps 'a configurable window' (singular) with no stated mapping from a per-rule window to a count. A rule asking for a longer window than the buffer silently under-counts.
findings.fix: Size the 1-second-slot ring to the max window any loaded rule requests (recomputed on reload) and expose countInWindow(name, sinceSec) summing the trailing slots; the engine passes each rule's withinSec/withinMin*60. State the over-buffer behavior (clamp+warn or size-to-max).

findings.title: restart overlimit counts toward both errored and restart-threshold, violating the stated 'at most one condition per event' invariant
findings.location: Event->MonitorEvents translation (restart overlimit), Error tracker (restart-window counter), alert-rule schema (disjointness claim)
findings.problem: errored fires on the transition reached via restart overlimit, AND the restart-window counter increments on restart overlimit and feeds restart-threshold. So one restart overlimit event maps to both conditions, contradicting the doc's claim that a single lifecycle event maps to at most one condition.
findings.fix: Pick one: (a) restart overlimit drives errored only and does not increment the restart-window counter; or (b) it contributes to both and the disjointness claim is narrowed to 'errored and unexpected-stop are disjoint', dropping the broader at-most-one-condition claim. Do not assert both.

findings.title: Name-keyed MonitorState map ignores PM2 duplicate names across pm_ids
findings.location: Core data model (Map<string,ProcessSnapshot> keyed by name), Aggregate semantics
findings.problem: PM2 permits two separately started fork apps to share a name; the name key collapses them. The design asserts name is a safe unique key without noting this exception.
findings.fix: State that duplicate names are treated as one aggregate (operators use unique names, documented in README) or warn on collision with last-writer-wins.

findings.title: GET /logs returns 200 empty for an unknown process, inconsistent with the 404 contract on process detail
findings.location: REST table (/logs), Log reading (readLogsTail returns {lines:[]}+200), Error-handling table
findings.problem: GET /api/processes/:name 404s for unknown names but /logs returns 200 {lines:[]}, conflating 'unknown process' with 'known process, no readable file'.
findings.fix: Resolve the process via the snapshot map first and 404 if the name is unknown; return 200 {lines:[]} only when the process exists but the file is missing/unreadable.

findings.title: sustainedAbove 'metric' selector is untyped; cpu/mem vs memory field-name mismatch risk
findings.problem: metric is clearly cpu|mem by context but never typed; a coder could pass 'memory' (ProcessSnapshot field) vs 'mem' (MetricSample field) and mismatch silently.
findings.fix: Type it metric: 'cpu' | 'mem' and note it indexes MetricSample, not ProcessSnapshot.

findings.title: Digest 'top error signatures over last 24h' has no backing store as specified
findings.location: Daily digest, Error tracker (ring buffer ERROR_BUFFER_SIZE; 1-second-slot windows)
findings.problem: The ring buffer holds recent distinct signatures (not 24h of occurrences) and TrackedError.count is all-time, not 24h; the sliding windows are per-process not per-signature. Exact 24h-windowed per-signature counts are not retained.
findings.fix: Redefine the digest metric as 'signatures whose lastSeen is within 24h, ranked by total count', and note it is an approximation bounded by ERROR_BUFFER_SIZE.

findings.title: EmailChannel.send(AlertPayload) cannot represent a multi-process digest; digest send path undefined
findings.location: Alert channels (EmailChannel.send(payload: AlertPayload)), Daily digest (sends through EmailChannel)
findings.problem: AlertPayload is single-process (processName/ruleId/severity required); the digest is a multi-process report that does not fit it, yet the digest 'sends it through the EmailChannel'.
findings.fix: Give EmailChannel a sendRaw({subject, html, text}) method (or define a DigestPayload) that the digest uses; state which so the channel interface is complete.
